recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-17219 unless the work group later reopens the separate question of how Observation patient chaining examples should be phrased.
issue_request: FHIR-17219 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core search correction for STU3. It reported that the second Advanced Filtering example was invalid because it searched the LOINC token with the name search parameter, and asked for the _filter expression to use code instead.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by git commit f003205a366f40f088e29f8e24abb09f3e9bf474, matching the Jira comment's svn 14264 reference. That commit changed source/search.html from _filter=name eq http://loinc.org|1234-5 to _filter=code eq http://loinc.org|1234-5.
additional_context: publish.ini lists search.html and search_filter.html as published pages. The current source/search.html example now uses code in both the ordinary search and _filter forms. Later Applied issue FHIR-45306 touched the same examples and changed the chain wording from subject.name to patient.name; that related issue is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source already satisfies FHIR-17219, and reverting the later patient.name wording would conflict with subsequent search-example clarification.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied clarification touched the same Advanced Filtering examples and explains why the current source uses patient.name rather than the older subject.name wording.
